first_impression.reaction: Good. It answers the question in the first paragraph and gives us one thing to do first: 'The one time that fixes everything else is sunset at your venue on your date, so look that up first and build the photos, the lighting and the reception entrance around it.' No 'dream day' rubbish, no hard sell. We're 14 months out with no destination yet, so an hour-by-hour run sheet is a little early for us, but this one is practical enough that I'd save it and send it to James.

journey.quote: The one time that fixes everything else is sunset at your venue on your date, so look that up first and build the photos, the lighting and the reception entrance around it.
journey.reaction: Clear, useful rule I hadn't thought of. Makes me trust the rest is worth skimming.

journey.section: A 4pm wedding timeline at a glance
journey.quote: Every clock time on this page is a planning example to adapt, not a rule.
journey.reaction: Appreciate the honesty. It doesn't pretend there's one perfect schedule.

journey.section: A 4pm wedding timeline without a first look
journey.quote: The cost is time with your guests, so ask the venue to hold canapés and a drink for you both, and keep the family photo list short and written down.
journey.reaction: An actual trade-off, stated plainly. This is the kind of thing that helps us decide on a first look rather than just telling us both options are lovely.

journey.section: How sunset shapes a 4pm wedding day
journey.quote: At a venue with hills, cliffs, trees or buildings to the west, the sun drops out of view before the listed time.
journey.reaction: Insider detail. Exactly the sort of thing we'd never think about until the photos come back dark.

journey.quote: So have the festoons, candles and uplights on before civil twilight ends, not after guests notice the dark.
journey.reaction: Practical. The twilight definitions are a bit technical for a skim, but this line translates them into something we can act on.

journey.section: Wedding day timeline for a 2pm ceremony
journey.quote: Guests travel in the late morning, so anyone arriving the same day has the least room for a delayed flight or a slow drive.
journey.reaction: This is our grandparents worry exactly. Half our guests are flying in, so this matters more to us than the light.

journey.section: Planning a 4pm ceremony at a destination wedding
journey.quote: What time will a 4pm ceremony be for family watching at home?
journey.reaction: Nice touch. We'd have relatives watching from Sydney if we go to Europe. This section feels written by someone who's actually done a destination wedding.

journey.section: Planning a 4pm ceremony at a destination wedding
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, works in your time zone, and is your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: Every planner says they're end-to-end. 'Single point of contact from start to finish' is the same line I've read on five other sites. After a section full of specific venue questions, this drops back into brochure language and doesn't connect to what I just read.

journey.quote: The first three lines come from the calculator for your venue and date.
journey.reaction: Useful. A template we'd actually copy into our shared sheet, though honestly we don't want to live in spreadsheets for 18 months.

journey.quote: For the feeling of the evening itself, browse [the Wedded Wonderland magazine]
journey.reaction: Third link in a row in that paragraph block. Slightly vague, but harmless. I'd probably click the magazine before the Concierge link, to see real weddings.

journey.section: Plan the day around your light
journey.quote: If you would like to work it through with someone, a Wedded Advisor agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: This is the line that actually speaks to our fear of hidden costs and currency surprises. Fee and inclusions in writing, quoted in AUD. I'd want this higher up, next to the first Advisor mention. Still no idea of the fee range though.

unanswered_questions: Is there a real wedding with a 4pm ceremony (venue and date) we can look at to see how this played out?
What does 'single point of contact from start to finish' actually include, and who is accountable if something goes wrong on the day itself?
Does the Advisor work with vendors they already know at the destination, or are they finding strangers?
Roughly what does a Wedded Advisor cost? The page says the fee is agreed in writing, but not a range.
How does this timeline change in countries where dinner normally starts late, for example if we chose Italy?
would_share_with: James (partner), mainly the first look versus no first look sections
Mum, for the destination questions about guests arriving the same day and the livestream time zone

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like to work it through with someone, a Wedded Advisor agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
cta_reaction.why: Not pushy, which I like, and the closing CTA addresses hidden costs. But we're early, we haven't picked a country, and we enquire after a couple of posts and at least one real wedding. Nothing here would stop us enquiring later; it just isn't enough on its own yet. The mid-article Advisor line reads like every other planner.

top_3_changes: Tie the mid-article Advisor line to the venue questions just listed, so it stops reading like generic 'end-to-end' planner copy (exact edit in suggested_edits[0]).
Add a question about older or less mobile guests to the destination checklist, since that is our biggest worry with international family (exact edit in suggested_edits[1]).
If the image register holds a real 4pm wedding with venue and date, link or caption it. A real example is what moves us from reading to enquiring. (No copy proposed; depends on what exists.)
